mainTopic: Yoma 41b: Bird offerings that become fixed by purchase, a rich person bringing a poor person's offering, and the red wool strips of the יום כפור goats and the פרה אדומה.
overview: The amud opens by defending רב חסדא's rule that bird offerings become fixed as חטאת or עולה only when the owner buys them. The גמרא changes the ברייתא's wording to 'he took and said.' It then rejects the idea that he redeemed a bird, because a bird offering cannot be redeemed. רב פפא explains that he bought only one of the two birds. Next, the גמרא returns to the dispute over whether a rich person who made the מקדש impure fulfills his obligation by bringing a poor person's offering. It shows from the verses ״תורת״, ״זאת״ and ״ואם דל הוא״ that the strict rule applies only to a מצורע. A new משנה then describes tying a red wool strip on the שעיר המשתלח and the כהן גדול's second וידוי over his פר. The גמרא proves from רב יוסף's ברייתא that the slaughtered goat also gets a strip, so the goats are never mixed up. Finally, the גמרא discusses the red strips of the פרה אדומה and the שעיר המשתלח: which one needs a minimum size, whether the strip needs weight, and what happens if the flame catches it early. The amud ends with three strips and three weights, and רבין's explanation of which weight goes with which strip continues on the next amud.

steps.title: According to the other version, how do we answer the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: In the version where רב ששת's explanation does not apply, the ברייתא seems to contradict רב חסדא. What answer is left?
steps.simpleTranslation: What can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב חסדא can be defended according to the version where the earlier answer does not work. This short question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that after setting money aside, the person said 'this is for my חטאת, this is for my עולה,' and those words had legal effect. That seems to show that speaking alone fixes the offering, which goes against רב חסדא. The question is how to save רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (an opening that asks how to resolve a problem)
Fixed designations: birds that have been assigned as חטאת or עולה
The owner's purchase. One of the two ways birds become fixed, according to רב חסדא

phrases.english: What can be said?
phrases.notes: This is asked on the version where the ברייתא is used to challenge רב חסדא, and רב ששת's way of reading it isn't available.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues from the earlier part of the daf, where רב ששת answered for one version of the sugya. This now asks about the other version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that birds become fixed only by the owner's purchase or the כהן's act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives legal force to a spoken assignment made after the money was set aside, so speaking alone seems to fix the offering.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'he took and said'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא so that it describes a case where he bought the birds and then spoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'and afterward he said.' Rather, say 'and afterward he took and said.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. Now the person actually bought the birds, and did not just make a statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new wording, the designation took effect through the owner's purchase. That is exactly what רב חסדא requires. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say... rather say (a formula for correcting a text)
He took, meaning he bought

phrases.english: Do not say: 'and afterward he said,'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: וְאַחַר כָּךְ לָקַח וְאָמַר.
phrases.english: rather say: 'and afterward he took (bought) and said.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר אֶלָּא אֵימָא וְאַחַר כָּךְ לָקַח וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that speaking alone fixes the birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a purchase that came with speech, so it fits רב חסדא.

steps.title: If he already bought the birds, what money is left to add to?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to say 'he adds and brings his obligation.' That makes no sense if he already spent the money on birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took (bought the birds), then 'he adds and brings his obligation', what is that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new wording. The rest of the ברייתא talks about adding to leftover money to buy a rich person's animal, but if he bought the birds, no money is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מוסיף ומביא חובתו' means he takes the חטאת money, adds more, and buys an animal. That only makes sense if he is still holding money. The new wording seems to remove that money, so the rest of the ברייתא no longer fits.

keyTerms.meaning: He adds more money and brings his obligation (the rich person's animal offering)
What is it? (here a challenge: what could this mean?)

phrases.english: If he took (bought), then 'he adds and brings his obligation'
what is that?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָקַח מוֹסִיף וּמֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מַאי נִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the corrected wording from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the birds are bought, no money remains to add to, so the ברייתא's ruling about adding money cannot apply.

steps.title: He redeemed the bird
steps.stepSummary: A suggested answer: he redeemed the bird and moved its holiness onto money, and that money is what he adds to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he redeems it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that he turned the bird back into money by redeeming it. Then he would have money to add to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redemption (פדיון) would move the bird's holiness onto money. That money could then go toward buying the animal. This would make 'he adds' fit the 'he bought' wording.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeems (moves holiness from an item onto money)

phrases.english: Where he redeems it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tries to answer the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He has no money left to add to.
steps.terutzMaskana: The redemption money is the money he adds to.

steps.title: Birds cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails, because a sanctified bird offering cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is no redemption for a bird!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the redemption idea. A bird that has been made holy as an offering can never be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha is that a bird offering has no פדיון. So the bird could not have been turned back into money, and the question from step 3 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (introduces a known fact that defeats a suggestion)
There is no redemption for a bird offering

phrases.english: But there is no redemption for a bird!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the answer in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The redemption explanation as a whole
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It depends on redeeming a bird, which the halacha does not allow.

steps.title: רב פפא: He bought only one bird
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that he bought only one of the two birds. The money for the other bird is still in his hand, and the ruling depends on which bird he bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For example, where he bought one single bird. If he bought the עולה bird, he adds to the money meant for his חטאת and brings his obligation, and this עולה bird goes to be a voluntary offering. If he bought the חטאת bird, he does not add to the money meant for his עולה to bring his obligation, and this חטאת bird is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא saves the corrected ברייתא by saying he bought only one bird, so some money is still left. He then explains both possibilities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he bought the עולה bird, the leftover money is חטאת money, so he can add to it and buy the animal חטאת a rich person owes. The bird becomes a voluntary נדבה. If he bought the חטאת bird, the leftover money is set aside for an עולה and cannot be used for his חטאת obligation. The bought חטאת bird is left to die, which is the rule for a חטאת that is no longer needed for atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: One single bird (out of the pair)
He bought
A voluntary offering
Goes to death: it is left to die and is not offered

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's rule stands. The ברייתא is about buying a single bird. If he bought the עולה bird, the leftover חטאת money goes toward the rich person's animal and the bird becomes a נדבה. If he bought the חטאת bird, the leftover עולה money cannot be used, and the bird is left to die.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Which bird he bought decides which kind of money is left over, and only leftover חטאת money can be used toward his חטאת obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רב חסדא's principle works in practice. Once a bird is fixed by purchase, it locks in what the remaining money is for.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, where he bought one single bird.
If he bought the burnt-offering bird,
he adds and brings his obligation from the money for his sin-offering,
and this burnt-offering goes to a voluntary offering.
If he bought the sin-offering bird,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹסִיף וּמֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִדְּמֵי עוֹלָתוֹ,
phrases.english: he does not add and bring his obligation from the money for his burnt-offering,
and this sin-offering goes to death (is left to die).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא כְּגוֹן שֶׁלָּקַח פְּרֵידָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the redemption answer was rejected in step 5, it gives a new answer to the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (only one bird was bought)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He took' means he bought both birds, so no money is left.
steps.terutzMaskana: He bought one bird, so the money for the second bird remains, and its use depends on which bird he bought.

steps.title: The dispute: a rich person who brings a poor person's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the dispute about a rich person who made the מקדש impure and brought a poor person's offering. רבי אלעזר quotes רבי הושעיא that he did not fulfill his obligation, and רבי חגא quotes him that he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main point. רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא: a rich person who made the מקדש impure and brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled his obligation. רבי חגא said in the name of רבי הושעיא: he has fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement it mentioned earlier and now looks at it directly. Two students report two opposite rulings in the name of the same teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who makes the מקדש impure brings a קרבן עולה ויורד, a 'sliding-scale' offering. A rich person brings an animal, and a poor person brings birds. The question is whether the cheaper, poor person's offering still counts if a rich person brings it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself' — back to the main statement mentioned earlier
Someone who enters the מקדש, or eats קדשים, while impure
The offering of a rich person (an animal) / the offering of a poor person (birds or flour)
He fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: We're going back to a statement quoted earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya:
A rich person who made the Temple impure
and brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חַגָּא אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא: יָצָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chaga said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya: he has fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about buying the birds and returns to the base dispute that was mentioned earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a rich person's use of a poor person's offering is invalid. רבי חגא: it is valid.

steps.title: Challenge from the law of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that a rich מצורע who brings a poor person's offering has not fulfilled his obligation. This seems to contradict רבי חגא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: a poor מצורע who brought a rich person's offering has fulfilled his obligation. A rich person who brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source about a מצורע to attack רבי חגא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע also brings an offering that changes based on wealth. The משנה says a rich person who brings the cheaper version has not fulfilled his obligation. If that is true for a מצורע, it should seem true for טומאת מקדש too, which goes against רבי חגא.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who brings offerings when he becomes pure

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מְצוֹרָע עָנִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר — יָצָא,
phrases.english: A poor leper who brought a rich person's offering has fulfilled his obligation;

phrases.aramaic: עָשִׁיר שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: a rich person who brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חגא's ruling from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חגא's view that a rich person fulfills his obligation with a poor person's offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel case of a מצורע, which also has an offering that changes based on wealth, rules that the rich person does not fulfill his obligation.

steps.title: A מצורע is different because of the word ״זאת״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the מצורע is a special case, because the Torah says ״זאת״ ('this'), which demands exactly what is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written ״זאת״ — 'this shall be the law of the מצורע.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חגא by saying the מצורע has its own special verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״זאת״ means the מצורע must do things exactly as stated, with no changes. That strict wording appears only by the מצורע, so its rule does not spread to טומאת מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is different there' — that case has a special reason
'This' — a word that teaches the procedure must be done exactly

phrases.english: It is different there,
because it is written: 'This.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יד:ב — 'This shall be the law of the leper.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases with a special verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule for a מצורע applies to every offering that changes based on wealth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע's strict rule comes from ״זאת״, a word that only appears there.

steps.title: Then the poor מצורע should also fail
steps.stepSummary: If ״זאת״ means no change at all, then the poor מצורע who brought the rich offering should also not fulfill his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first part of the משנה should also be invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת״ seems to block any change, in either direction. But the first part of the משנה says a poor מצורע who brings the rich offering has fulfilled his obligation. So why does ״זאת״ not make that invalid as well?

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so' — if your explanation is correct
The first part of the source

phrases.english: If so, the first clause too should be invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the ״זאת״ answer from step 9 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״זאת״ as a demand for exactness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״זאת״ blocks every change, it should block the poor person bringing more, not only the rich person bringing less.

steps.title: ״תורת״ includes the poor מצורע, and ״זאת״ excludes the rich one
steps.stepSummary: The word ״תורת״ adds the case of a poor מצורע who brings the rich offering. ״זאת״ then excludes the rich person who brings the poor offering, as a ברייתא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah included that case with the word ״תורת״. As a ברייתא teaches: ״תורת״ comes to include a poor מצורע who brought a rich person's offering. You might think that even a rich person who brought a poor person's offering is included, so the verse says ״זאת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a second word in the same verse, and supports this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has two words that pull in two directions. ״תורת״ widens the rule so that a poor person who brings more is valid. ״זאת״ narrows it so that a rich person who brings less is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One (the Torah) included'
'The law of' — a word used to include an extra case
'The verse teaches' — introducing the verse that settles the question

steps.whatToRemember: By a מצורע: a poor person who brings the rich offering is valid (״תורת״), but a rich person who brings the poor offering is invalid (״זאת״).

phrases.english: But the Merciful One included it with 'the law of,'
as it was taught in a baraita: 'The law of'

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת מְצוֹרָע עָנִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר.
phrases.english: comes to include a poor leper who brought a rich person's offering.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ עָשִׁיר שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי —
phrases.english: One might think that even a rich person who brought a poor person's offering is valid,
therefore the verse states: 'This.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 10 and backs the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second word in the verse adds the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זאת״ alone would invalidate any change, in either direction.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תורת״ includes the poor person who brings more, so ״זאת״ only excludes the rich person who brings less.

steps.title: Let us learn טומאת מקדש from the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we do not copy the מצורע's rule (a rich person with a poor offering is invalid) onto טומאת מקדש, which would go against רבי חגא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חגא again: perhaps the מצורע's rule is a model for every offering that changes based on wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if ״זאת״ is written only by the מצורע, maybe it teaches a general rule that we should apply to the similar offering of טומאת מקדש. If so, the rich person there would also not fulfill his obligation, against רבי חגא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us learn from it' — apply one case's rule to another

phrases.english: But let us derive the law from it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the rule is written by the מצורע, but asks why it should not spread to טומאת מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חגא's ruling, and the claim that the מצורע is a separate case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Similar offerings should share rules, so the מצורע's strictness should apply to טומאת מקדש.

steps.title: ״ואם דל הוא״ limits the strict rule to the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The Torah limited the rule with ״ואם דל הוא״. The word ״הוא״ ('he') shows the strictness applies only to the מצורע, so רבי חגא's ruling stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One excluded it with ״ואם דל הוא״ — 'and if he is poor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a word in the מצורע section blocks us from copying its rule to other offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״הוא״ points to the מצורע alone: only for him must the poor offering be brought by an actually poor person. Other wealth-based offerings, like טומאת מקדש, are not included, so a rich person there can fulfill his obligation with a poor person's offering, as רבי חגא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Torah excluded' — a word that limits a rule
'And if he is poor' (ויקרא יד:כא); ״הוּא״ limits the rule to this case

steps.whatToRemember: The strict rule (a rich person bringing a poor offering is invalid) belongs to the מצורע alone, because of ״זאת״ and ״הוא״. This leaves room for רבי חגא's view by טומאת מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: ״הוא״ does not teach anything new about the poor מצורע himself. Its job is to stop the מצורע's strict rule from spreading to other offerings.

phrases.english: The Merciful One excluded it
with 'and if he is poor.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יד:כא. The word 'he' shows that only this person, the מצורע, is limited this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12, blocking the comparison between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע's rule should apply to every offering that changes based on wealth.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״הוא״ limits the rule to the מצורע, so טומאת מקדש can follow רבי חגא.

steps.title: The red strip and placing the two goats
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the כהן גדול ties a red wool strip on the head of the שעיר המשתלח. He stands it facing the place it will be sent out from. The goat to be slaughtered is placed facing the place where it will be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He tied a strip of red wool on the head of the goat that is sent away. He stood it facing the place it would be sent out from. And for the goat to be slaughtered, he stood it facing the place where it would be slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how the two goats are marked and placed after the lottery (גורל).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two actions are done to the שעיר המשתלח: tying the red strip and standing it in place. The משנה then adds a short phrase about the second goat, ״ולנשחט״. It does not say clearly which of the two actions that phrase includes, and this gap will become the גמרא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip ('tongue') of red/crimson wool
The goat sent away to עזאזל
The place (gate) from which it is sent out
The goat that is slaughtered (the goat for ה׳)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the משנה says only ״ולנשחט — כנגד בית שחיטתו״. It never says outright whether the slaughtered goat also gets a red strip. That missing detail is exactly what the גמרא will ask about.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: He tied a strip of crimson wool
on the head of the goat that is sent away,
and stood it facing the place it is sent out from,
and the slaughtered one — facing the place of its slaughter.
phrases.notes: This phrase is unclear: does it refer to tying, standing, or both?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the earlier discussion about מצורע and קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A red strip is tied on the שעיר המשתלח's head. Each goat is stood facing the place where its service will happen.

steps.title: The second confession over the bull
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול returns to his פר a second time. He leans both hands on it and confesses for himself, his household, and all the כהנים. The people answer ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He comes to his bull a second time. He leans his two hands on it and confesses. This is what he would say: 'Please, ה׳! I have sinned, done wrong, and rebelled before You, I and my household and the sons of אהרן, Your holy people. Please, ה׳, forgive the wrongs, rebellions, and sins that I did before You, I and my household and the sons of אהרן, Your holy people. As it is written in the Torah of משה Your servant: "For on this day He will atone for you to purify you from all your sins; before ה׳ you will be pure."' And they answer after him: 'Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the next part of the עבודה. The כהן גדול does a second וידוי on his own פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first וידוי on the פר was only for himself and his household. This second one adds ״ובני אהרן עם קדושך״, so it also atones for all the כהנים. Each time he says the שם המפורש, the people answer ״ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד״.

keyTerms.meaning: Leans his hands on the animal (סמיכה)
Confesses sins (וידוי)
His bull — the כהן גדול's own חטאת
The כהנים, descendants of אהרן
The people's response when they hear the שם

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the פר of the כהן גדול atones in stages. The first וידוי covers him and his household. The second also includes the whole family of כהנים.

phrases.english: He comes to his bull a second time,
and leans his two hands on it and confesses,
and this is what he would say: Please, ה׳!
(I have sinned, done wrong, and rebelled) before You,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי וּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן עַם קְדוֹשֶׁךָ.
phrases.english: I and my household and the sons of Aharon, Your holy people.
Please, ה׳! Please forgive
the wrongs, and the rebellions, and the sins
that I did wrong, rebelled, and sinned before You,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי וּבֵיתִי וּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן עַם קְדוֹשֶׁךָ,
phrases.english: I and my household and the sons of Aharon, Your holy people,
as it is written in the Torah of Moshe Your servant:
"For on this day He will atone for you
to purify you from all your sins;
before ה׳ you will be pure,"
and they answer after him:
"Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with the next step of the עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second וידוי on the פר is said with סמיכה. It covers the כהן גדול, his household, and all the כהנים.

steps.title: Does 'and the slaughtered one' refer to tying or to standing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ״ולנשחט״ in the משנה refers to. One option is that the slaughtered goat also gets a red strip, tied at its neck where it will be slaughtered. The other option is that it is only stood facing its place of slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: When the משנה says "and for the slaughtered one," does it refer back to the tying? Or does it refer back to the standing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question (איבעיא) about how to read the משנה. It is asking which action ״ולנשחט״ connects to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״ולנשחט״ goes with the tying, the slaughtered goat also gets a strip, tied around its neck. If it goes with the standing, the slaughtered goat only gets placed opposite its place of slaughter, with no strip. The question is about wording, but the answer decides a practical detail of the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked / a question was raised (a true open question)
Tying (of the red strip)
Standing / positioning the animal
Refers to / stands on

phrases.english: GEMARA: They asked:
"And the slaughtered one" — does it refer to the tying,
or does it refer to the standing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the unclear phrase at the end of step 14's משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the slaughtered goat also gets a red strip (tying), or is only positioned facing its place of slaughter (standing).

steps.title: רב יוסף's ברייתא: so the goats do not get mixed up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רב יוסף. It repeats the משנה's words and adds a reason: so the two goats do not mix with each other, and do not mix with other goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, from what רב יוסף taught: He tied a strip of red wool on the head of the goat that is sent away, and stood it facing the place it is sent from. And for the slaughtered one, facing its place of slaughter. This is so that one should not get mixed up with the other, and so they should not get mixed up with other goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. This step sets up the proof: the key piece is the reason the ברייתא gives, and the גמרא will draw its conclusion from that reason next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds something the משנה did not say: the purpose is to prevent mix-ups. A strip on each goat (one on the head, one on the neck) would clearly tell them apart and keep them separate from other goats. Just standing them in a place would not do this as well, since animals move. This reason points toward reading ״ולנשחט״ as going with the tying.

keyTerms.meaning: That רב יוסף taught (a ברייתא)
So that it should not become mixed up
Other (goats)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא repeats the משנה word for word. Its only new part is the reason at the end (״שלא יתערב״). That reason is what makes it a proof.

phrases.english: Come and hear, from what Rav Yosef taught:
He tied a strip of crimson wool
on the head of the goat that is sent away,
and stood it facing the place it is sent out from,
and the slaughtered one — facing the place of its slaughter,
so that one should not get mixed up with the other,
and they should not get mixed up with others.
phrases.notes: The proof from this reason continues in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question asked in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: Whether ״ולנשחט״ refers to the tying, so the slaughtered goat also gets a strip.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא, which explains the purpose as preventing mix-ups. This fits best with tying a marker on both goats.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא proves the slaughtered goat is also tied
steps.stepSummary: Only if both goats get a strip can neither goat be mixed up with other goats. So ״ולנשחט״ refers to tying.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the ברייתא is talking about tying, that works well. But if you say it is only talking about standing the goat in place, there is a problem. True, the two goats will not get mixed up with each other, because this one has a strip and that one does not. But the untied goat could still get mixed up with other goats! So we must learn from this that it is talking about tying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב יוסף's ברייתא answers the question from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the reason is so the goats do not mix with each other and do not mix with other goats. If only the שעיר המשתלח had a strip, the slaughtered goat would look like any ordinary goat and could easily get mixed up with them. So the slaughtered goat must also have its own strip, tied at its neck.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it works out fine (opens the side that works)
Tying (of the red strip)
Standing it in place (positioning the goat)
Gets mixed up
Granted that... (admits one point before raising a problem)

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא אַקְּשִׁירָה קָאֵי — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it refers to tying, it works well.
But if you say it refers to positioning,
granted it would not get mixed up with its partner,
phrases.notes: Its partner means the other goat of the pair.

phrases.english: since this one has a strip tied to it
and that one does not have a strip tied to it,
but it could at least get mixed up with other goats!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַקְּשִׁירָה קָאֵי.
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it that it refers to tying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from Step 17 settles the question from Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That ״ולנשחט״ in the משנה means the slaughtered goat also gets a red strip tied at its neck.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא: the goats must not mix with each other or with other goats.

steps.title: Conclusion: the slaughtered goat is tied too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof. The goat to be slaughtered also gets a red strip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the question from Step 16. Both goats get strips. The שעיר המשתלח gets one on its head, and the slaughtered goat gets one at its neck.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Both goats get a red wool strip. The שעיר המשתלח gets it on its head, and the goat for slaughter gets it at its neck. This way they are never mixed up with each other or with any other goats.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof of Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״ולנשחט״ refers to tying. The slaughtered goat also gets a red strip, at its neck.

steps.title: רבי יצחק forgot which red strip needs a minimum size
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק heard that one red strip needs a שיעור and one does not. He does not remember which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: I heard a teaching about two strips of red wool. One is the strip of the פרה אדומה, and one is the strip of the שעיר המשתלח. One of them needs a minimum size, and one does not need a minimum size. But I do not know which is which.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about red wool strips. רבי יצחק reports a teaching but has forgotten an important detail. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Red wool is used in two places: it is thrown into the fire of the פרה אדומה, and it is tied to the שעיר המשתלח. רבי יצחק knows that only one of them has a minimum size. He does not know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: Strips (literally 'tongues') of wool
The red heifer (פרה אדומה)
Minimum required size or amount
And I do not know

steps.confusionAlert: Here לשונות does not mean 'versions of a teaching.' It means physical strips of red wool, shaped like tongues.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
I heard about two strips,
one of the red heifer,
and one of the scapegoat.
One requires a minimum size,
and one does not require a minimum size.
But I do not know which of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שְׁתֵּי לְשׁוֹנוֹת שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the red strip from Steps 14 to 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the two red strips (פרה and שעיר המשתלח), one needs a שיעור and one does not. Which one is unknown.

steps.title: רב יוסף reasons that the scapegoat's strip needs a minimum size
steps.stepSummary: The strip of the שעיר המשתלח gets cut in two, so it needs a שיעור. The strip of the פרה is not cut, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Let us figure it out ourselves. The strip of the שעיר המשתלח has to be divided, so it needs a minimum size. The strip of the פרה does not have to be divided, so it does not need a minimum size.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף uses logic to solve רבי יצחק's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the שעיר המשתלח is pushed off the cliff, its strip is cut in half. One half is tied to a rock and the other half between its horns. A strip that must be split needs to be long enough for two usable pieces. The פרה's strip is simply thrown into the fire whole, so no size is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see for ourselves (let us reason it out)
Division, cutting into two
Requires / needs

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Let us see for ourselves:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ דְּבָעֵי חֲלוּקָּה — בָּעֵי שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: the strip of the scapegoat, which needs dividing, needs a minimum size,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל פָּרָה דְּלָא בָּעֵי חֲלוּקָּה — לָא בָּעֵי שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: and that of the heifer, which does not need dividing, does not need a minimum size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt raised by רבי יצחק in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two red strips needs a שיעור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שעיר המשתלח's strip needs a שיעור because it is divided. The פרה's strip does not, because it is not divided.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the heifer's strip also needs weight
steps.stepSummary: The פרה's strip must be heavy enough to fall into the fire, so it should also need a שיעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged this: The strip of the פרה also needs weight!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב יוסף's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The red wool is thrown into the fire of the burning פרה. If it is too light, it might blow away instead of landing in the fire. So it must have some heaviness, which means a minimum size. Then רב יוסף's way of telling the two strips apart falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objected to it
Weight, heaviness
Also

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama strongly objected:
The heifer's strip also needs weight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the פרה's strip needs no שיעור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרה's strip must be heavy enough to fall into the fire. Weight requires size, so it too needs a שיעור.

steps.title: רבא: the weight requirement is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: Whether the פרה's strip needs weight is a מחלוקת תנאים. רב יוסף follows the view that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The rule about weight is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב יוסף against רמי בר חמא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that the פרה's strip must be heavy. Some תנאים hold it needs weight, and some hold it does not. רב יוסף follows the view that no weight is needed, so his reasoning still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, the red strip of the שעיר המשתלח needs a minimum size because it is cut in two. The strip of the פרה does not need one. Whether the פרה's strip must be heavy is a מחלוקת תנאים, and רב יוסף holds it does not.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Weight is a dispute among the Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: כּוֹבֶד תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's objection in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the premise to one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees the פרה's strip needs weight, so it must also need a שיעור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weight requirement is disputed. רב יוסף follows the תנא who holds no weight is needed.

steps.title: אביי challenges the claim that the heifer's strip is never cut
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה that speaks of 'the leftovers of the strip' when burning the פרה. That wording suggests the strip was cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that the strip of the פרה does not need to be divided? אביי challenged this: How does he do it? He wraps them with the leftovers of the strip!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 21, which said the פרה's strip is never cut. אביי quotes a משנה that seems to show it is cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained that the strip of the שעיר המשתלח needs a שיעור because it gets cut in two, and the פרה's strip does not. The משנה says the כהן wraps the cedar and אזוב with the 'שיירי לשון' (leftovers of the strip). Leftovers only exist if part of the strip was cut off, so it seems the פרה's strip is also divided.

keyTerms.meaning: Dividing; cutting into parts
He wraps them together
The leftovers of the strip

phrases.english: And the [strip] of the heifer does not need dividing?!
phrases.notes: A shocked question aimed at step 21

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
How does he do it?
phrases.notes: Quoting a משנה in מסכת פרה

phrases.english: He wraps them with the leftovers of the strip!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the distinction made in step 21 and challenges it from a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרה's strip is never cut and so needs no שיעור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'leftovers' implies the strip was divided, just like the שעיר המשתלח's strip

steps.title: Change the wording to 'the end of the strip'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the משנה's wording from 'leftovers of the strip' to 'the tail end of the strip.' No cutting is implied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: with the tail end of the strip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by changing one word in the משנה so that it no longer implies cutting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Leftovers' implies a piece was removed. 'Tail end' just means the loose end of a whole strip that is used for tying. With this wording, the distinction from step 21 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (change the wording)
The tail end of the strip

steps.confusionAlert: 'אימא' here does not add a new opinion. It changes the reading of the משנה's wording so the problem goes away.

phrases.english: Say: with the tail end of the strip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says 'leftovers,' so the strip must have been cut
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'tail end.' The strip is whole and is not divided

steps.title: רב: it is valid if the flame catches the cedar and strip early
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין quotes רב: if the cedar wood and red strip are caught by the flame before they reach the burning פרה, the פרה is still כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said in the name of רב: Cedar wood and the red strip that a flame caught are כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. It is about what happens if the items thrown into the fire burn up in the air before they land on the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says to throw the cedar, אזוב and red strip 'into the burning of the פרה.' רב rules that if the flame rising from the פרה grabs them on the way, this is good enough. They do not have to physically land in the middle of the burning animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Cedar wood
The red (crimson) wool strip
That the flame caught
Valid

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said that Rav said:
Cedar wood and the crimson strip
that a flame caught: it is valid.
phrases.notes: They burned in the air before reaching the פרה itself

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new but related topic: burning the red strip together with the פרה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the flame catches the cedar and red strip before they reach the burning פרה, it is כשרה

steps.title: A ברייתא says a singed strip must be replaced
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the strip got singed, a new strip must be brought. This seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If the strip was singed, he brings another strip and makes it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says a strip burned by the flame before reaching the פרה is fine. The ברייתא says a strip that got singed does not count and must be replaced. The two sources seem to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Was singed or scorched
And makes it holy (by burning it properly with the פרה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If the strip was singed,
he brings another strip and sanctifies it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a strip caught by the flame early is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a singed strip does not count and needs replacing

steps.title: אביי: it depends on the kind of flame
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two sources describe different flames. A tall flame far above the פרה does not count. A low flame close to the פרה does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here it is a high-shooting flame; there it is a low, bending flame.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the flame shoots high, so the strip burns far from the פרה and is not 'in the burning of the פרה.' In רב's case, the flame is low and close to the פרה, so burning in it counts as burning with the פרה. Both rulings are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
A flame shooting up high
A flame bending low, close to the pile

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
Here with a high-blazing flame, there with a low-bending flame.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a high flame, so it's invalid; רב means a low flame, so it's valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּקוֹלַחַת, כָּאן בְּנִכְפֶּפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between רב and the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא disagree about any strip burned by the flame
steps.terutzMaskana: A low flame near the פרה counts; a high flame far from it does not

steps.title: רבא: it is a dispute about weight
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. רב and the ברייתא follow two sides of a מחלוקת תנאים about whether the bundle needs weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Weight is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers another way to settle the contradiction. Here he only states his claim, and the next step brings his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bundle must have weight so that it falls into the middle of the burning פרה, then a strip burned in the air does not count, as the ברייתא says. If no weight is needed, then the flame catching it is enough, as רב says. So רבא does not split the cases. He says the two sources follow different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Weight
It is a dispute among the תנאים

phrases.english: Rava says: Weight is a dispute of tanna'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the contradiction, different from אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא must agree, so one of them seems wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא holds that weight is needed; רב follows the view that it is not
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same מחלוקת mentioned in step 23. It shows that one dispute about weight explains two separate issues in this סוגיא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: why the items are wrapped together
steps.stepSummary: רבי says they are wrapped to make one bundle. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is to give them weight so they fall into the burning פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Why does he wrap them? So that they will all be in one bundle. These are the words of רבי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: So that they will have weight and fall into the burning of the פרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבא's claim that there really is a מחלוקת about weight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, wrapping is only about keeping all three items together, so weight does not matter and רב's ruling fits. According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, wrapping exists to give weight so the items land in the fire, so the ברייתא that requires a new strip fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: One bundle
The burning of the פרה

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to רב versus the ברייתא: אביי says it depends on whether the flame is high or low. רבא says it depends on whether the bundle needs weight, which is a dispute between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Why does he wrap them?

steps.title: Three crimson strips with three different weights
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that there are three crimson strips: one for the פרה אדומה, one for the שעיר המשתלח, and one for the מצורע. Their weights are ten זוז, two סלעים, and one שקל. However, רבי יוחנן cannot say which weight goes with which strip.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: I heard about three crimson strips. One is used for the פרה אדומה, one for the שעיר המשתלח, and one for the מצורע. One weighs ten זוז, one weighs two סלעים, and one weighs a שקל. But I cannot explain which weight belongs to which strip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. Each of the three crimson strips has its own fixed weight, but the person who heard the teaching does not know how the weights match up with the strips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier discussion, since it shows that crimson strips really do have set weights. We now know three weights and three strips. What is missing is which weight belongs to which strip. רבי יוחנן openly admits he does not know, and that leaves room for someone else to fill in the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip, here a strip of crimson wool. It does not mean 'tongue' or 'language' in this context.
The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כפור
A person with צרעת, who uses a crimson strip in the purification process
A coin and unit of weight
A coin worth 4 זוז, so two סלעים equal 8 זוז
Here, half a סלע, which is 2 זוז

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read לשונות as 'languages.' Here it means strips of crimson wool. Also, the three weights are all different: ten זוז, then eight זוז (two סלעים), then two זוז (a שקל).

steps.title: רבין arrives to explain which weight goes with which strip
steps.stepSummary: רבין comes from ארץ ישראל and explains, in the name of רבי יונתן, how the three weights match the three strips. The actual explanation follows on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he explained it in the name of רבי יונתן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to give the missing explanation that רבי יוחנן could not give, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן left a gap: which weight goes with which strip. רבין now brings a tradition from a different teacher, רבי יונתן, that fills in that gap. So this step answers the open question from step 31, but the answer itself has not been stated yet.
